correctness.rationale: Every finite concept is enumerated by exact independence and domination constraints over every subset of n vertices. The VC test enumerates every support, and the complete first-query minimax recurrence computes exact Littlestone depth. Two independently implemented algorithms produce identical results in all 24 connected path/cycle cases through 13 vertices. Explicit 16- and 32-leaf adaptive certificates replay completely for P10 and C13; their family sizes 16 and 39 strictly forbid one further complete level. Degree-two decomposition and product additivity prove the 10-vertex uniqueness and infinite disjoint-union formula. No connected claim is extrapolated beyond the checked cases.

originality.rationale: The identifiable closest sources do not assert or logically entail the first degree-two adaptive threshold, its unique ten-vertex example, or the first cyclic threshold. Malliaris-Moran treat general Littlestone classes; Palmer-Patkos count maximal independent sets; Liu et al. Lemma 2.20 gives a nonadaptive VC upper bound. Relevant prior graph-specific claims give a first branching example and an exact forest VC criterion, neither of which determines adaptive ranks for paths or cycles. Searches of published published-finding corpus claims did not locate equivalent coverage. Residual historical-priority risk is acknowledged, not treated as proof of absolute novelty.
residual_risks: Broader unindexed literature may contain the same finite thresholds or stronger general results.

value.rationale: The first degree-two adaptive gap distinguishes branch-dependent constructions from genuine low-degree phenomena, and the first cycle gap isolates the same behavior in regular degree-two structures. Both are exact natural minimal-order boundaries, supported by complete classification of all smaller paths/cycles. The path construction yields an unlimited adaptive-vs-static dimension gap while forbidding any degree-three branching, a structural strengthening unavailable from the earlier general-forest witness.
